big: A PMS charges 2% a year on ₹1 crore. That is ₹2 lakh, whether or not the portfolio gains. Add a profit share, brokerage and taxes. Fees quietly reduce returns, so read them first.

lines: A share of profits above an agreed return, called the hurdle. A high-water mark means no fee until the portfolio passes its earlier peak. The management fee is separate: a fixed percentage every year.

note: After a fall, no profit share is charged until the portfolio is above its earlier peak.

title: PMS fees
stops: A management fee is charged regardless of performance
A performance fee is charged on all returns from the first rupee
A hurdle rate must be beaten first
A high-water mark charges fees on recovered losses

q: A PMS charges 2% of the portfolio value every year. What fee is this?
why: A performance fee depends on profits. The details here point elsewhere.
It is a fixed percentage regardless of performance.
A hurdle rate is a return threshold. It does not fit the facts given.
A custody fee is for safekeeping. It does not fit the facts given.

q: A manager earns a profit share only on returns above 10% a year. What is the 10%?
why: The management fee is a percentage of assets.
An exit load is charged on early exit.
A benchmark is an index for comparison.
It is the minimum return before a performance fee.

q: After a fall, no profit share is charged until the portfolio passes its earlier peak. What is this?
why: A hurdle is a minimum return.
A margin call is for futures.
It charges only above the previous peak.
Lot size is a contract quantity.

q: A manager takes 20% of gains beyond a set hurdle. What is this called?
why: It is a share of profits above a hurdle.
A management fee is a fixed percentage.
A custody fee is for safekeeping.
A tax is paid to the government.

pts: Management fee: fixed %, regardless of performance.
Performance fee: share of gains above the hurdle rate.
High-water mark: no fee until the earlier peak is passed.
